The lower esophageal sphincter (LES), which lies above the 
entrance to the stomach, prevents reflux of gastric contents 
into the esophagus. The pyloric sphincter in the distal portion 
of the stomach helps regulate the exit of gastric contents, pre-
venting backflow of chyme from the duodenum into the stom-
ach. Obesity, certain food, gastrointestinal regulators, and ir-
ritation from nearby ulcers may alter the performance of 
sphincters. Certain foods and beverages may alter LES pres-
sure, permitting reflux of stomach contents back into the 
esophagus (see Chapter 27).
The stomach continuously mixes and churns food and nor-
mally releases the mixture in small quantities into the small 
intestine through the pyloric sphincter. The amount emptied 
with each contraction of the antrum and pylorus varies with 
the volume and type of food consumed, but only a few millili-
ters are released at a time. The presence of acid and nutrients in 
the duodenum stimulate the regulatory hormone, GIP, to slow 
gastric emptying.
